{{Field procedure|summary=Map a planetary ring with a Detailed Surface Scanner and use the resulting hotspot markers to choose a mining search area.}}

Use this procedure after reaching a ringed body and before selecting a location for a [[Mining|mining]] run. A hotspot identifies a region where its named commodity is more likely to be encountered; it does not mark an individual valuable asteroid.<ref name="frontier-beyond">[https://www.elitedangerous.com/en-US/news/elite-dangerous-beyond-chapter-four-out-now Elite Dangerous: Beyond – Chapter Four – Out Now], Frontier Developments, 11 December 2018. Accessed 10 September 2026.</ref>

== Before you start ==

* Fit and power a [[Detailed Surface Scanner]].
* Assign '''Surface Scanner''' to a fire group.
* Identify a body with [[Planetary Rings|planetary rings]] and approach it in Supercruise.
* Know which commodity or mining method the run is intended to use. [[Mining Hotspot|Hotspot]] names guide the search, but ring type and mining method still matter.

== Procedure ==

{{Procedure steps|
# Target the ringed body and remain in Supercruise.
# Switch to '''Analysis Mode''' and activate the Surface Scanner when the body is within range.
# Aim a probe directly at the visible ring. The projected path must intersect the ring rather than only the planet.
# Fire the probe and wait for the ring scan to complete. One valid ring impact reveals the hotspot regions in that ring system.<ref name="dss-community">[https://elite-dangerous.fandom.com/wiki/Detailed_Surface_Scanner Detailed Surface Scanner], Elite Dangerous Wiki. Accessed 10 September 2026.</ref>
# Close the DSS and inspect the revealed hotspot markers in the navigation display.
# Select a hotspot matching the intended commodity and mining method.
# Approach the marker in Supercruise, then drop into the ring at a safe distance from the hotspot centre or at the planned overlap location.
# Begin the appropriate prospecting and extraction procedure. The hotspot narrows the search area; it does not identify which asteroid contains the target material.
}}

A ring scan and a planetary-body map are separate results. A probe can scan the ring without fully mapping the planet or moon it surrounds.

== Interpreting the result ==

* '''Named hotspot:''' a broad region associated with a mined commodity. It improves targeting but does not guarantee that every asteroid contains that commodity.
* '''Overlapping hotspots:''' overlapping regions may be useful when the chosen mining plan specifically calls for that combination, but an overlap is not required for ordinary mining.
* '''No useful hotspot:''' the ring may still contain mineable asteroids. Move to another ring when the run depends on a specific hotspot.
* '''Several ring bands:''' make sure the probe intersects the band you intend to mine; separate bands can return separate hotspot layouts.

Continue with [[Laser Mining]], [[Core Mining]], [[Sub-surface Mining]], or another method listed on [[Mining]].

== Completion check ==

The procedure is complete when the intended ring band has been scanned, its hotspot markers are visible, and a suitable marker has been selected—or when the scan confirms that the ring has no useful hotspot for the current plan.

== Common problems ==

* '''Only the planet was mapped:''' aim the probe path at the ring itself. A surface impact on the body does not scan the ring.
* '''The probe misses:''' use the trajectory indicator and adjust the aim until the projected path crosses the visible ring band.
* '''No hotspot markers appear:''' confirm that the probe struck the ring and that the correct ringed body is still selected.
* '''The desired commodity is absent:''' check another ring rather than assuming every ring supports every mined commodity.
* '''The marker is far away:''' target it and travel in Supercruise before dropping into the ring.
* '''The hotspot name looked profitable but the sale was poor:''' hotspot selection affects acquisition, not current market demand or price. Check a current market source before committing the run.
* '''No valuable asteroid is visible at the marker:''' hotspots identify search regions. Use prospectors and the equipment appropriate to the selected mining method.
